_comment: The six App Store screenshot slots, in order. Order matters more than polish:
people swipe two or three and stop.
`capture` names a PNG in ./captures. Any aspect works; it is drawn to fill
the frame from the top, so a tall iPhone 14 grab (1170x2532) is fine.
`kind` is 'device' for a normal caption-over-app slot, or 'statement' for one
that carries a large claim with the app dimmed behind it.

slots.caption:
Photograph a receipt.
It is read on your phone.
slots.sub: Merchant, date, total and tax category, in about a second

slots.caption:
Nothing leaves
this device.
claims: No cloud, no sync, no server
Read and categorized by your iPhone
slots.sub: Your receipts are a database on this phone. The only way anything leaves is an export you perform.

slots.caption:
29 categories,
mapped to real IRS lines.
slots.sub: Schedule C, Schedule A, Form 8829, 4562 and cost of goods sold

slots.caption:
Your year,
by Schedule C line.
slots.sub: Business and personal kept apart, with sales tax tracked separately

slots.caption:
Hand your CPA
a file they can open.
slots.sub: CSV, Excel, TXF for tax software, QuickBooks Online, or a full archive

slots.caption:
One receipt,
two categories.
slots.sub: Sales tax divided the way the amounts were, down to the cent
